title: [WIP] Proposal: Add multi source urls to script and links to provide better caching coverage
body: When including a common resource using a hyperlink or script tag, a CDN host may be used to make use of an already cached resource loaded on request of a different web page. There are however multiple CDN hosts, potentially serving the same resource without it being transparent to the browser that the resource requested at host A is already cached for host B. For example: - Web page 1 requests resource X at host A - Web page 2 requests resource X at host B While the resource is identical between host A and B, the resource is downloaded and cached twice, and the load time for web page 2 is longer than necessary. This PR proposes to change the src attribute of script elements and href attribute of link elements from accepting a single argument to multiple. When one of the urls provided is already cached for a resource, that cached resource is used (provided the cached resource is not stale etc.) When none of the resources at the urls provided is already cached, the first url is used to download the resource. Because the urls should serve the same resource, and the developer may inadvertently provide urls to different resources, the integrity attribute should always be set when the src or href attribute contain multiple urls. This integrity attribute is used to check the downloaded resources, but also checked against any cached resource to make sure no incorrect resource is loaded. An example after this proposal is accepted: - Web page 1 requests resource X with integrity "fooBar" at either host A, B or C. Resource X is not cached yet, so downloaded from host A. - Web page 2 requests resource X with integrity "fooBar" at either host B, A or D. Resource X is cached for host A with integrity "fooBar", so that resource is used. - Web page 3 requests resource X with integrity "fooBar" at host B. Resource X is cached for host A with the same integrity "fooBar" but not cached for host B yet, so the resource is downloaded again and the resource of host B is used. (Same as current implementations) - Web page 4 requests resource X with integrity "barFoo" at host A. The resource is cached for the exact same url, but the integrity doesn't match. An error is thrown. - Web page 5 requests resource X with integrity "barFoo" at host D. The resource is not cached for this url, so downloaded. The integrity doesn't match, so an error is thrown. (Current implementation). Btw, I am not familiar with introducing a proposal, so I hope this is the correct way to introduce it.
